cards.explanation: The recipient mounts an immune response to an antigen and can develop immunological memory.
cards.question: Vaccination induces artificially acquired {{c1::active immunity}}.

cards.explanation: The aim is to establish protection before exposure causes illness.
cards.text: Vaccination given to prevent disease is described as {{c1::prophylactic}}.
cards.question: Vaccination given to prevent disease is described as {{c1::prophylactic}}.

cards.explanation: A useful response must also recognise the relevant antigen on later exposure.
cards.text: A vaccine’s capacity to elicit an immune response is called {{c1::immunogenicity}}.
cards.question: A vaccine’s capacity to elicit an immune response is called {{c1::immunogenicity}}.

cards.explanation: This can support a strong immune response. Suitability depends on the vaccine and the recipient.
cards.text: A live attenuated vaccine can provide sustained antigen exposure because the weakened organism can {{c1::replicate}}.
cards.question: A live attenuated vaccine can provide sustained antigen exposure because the weakened organism can {{c1::replicate}}.

cards.explanation: Antigens can still be recognised by the immune system.
cards.text: An inactivated whole-organism vaccine contains microbes that {{c1::cannot replicate}}.
cards.question: An inactivated whole-organism vaccine contains microbes that {{c1::cannot replicate}}.

cards.explanation: It retains antigenic features that allow antibodies to recognise the toxin.
cards.text: A vaccine antigen derived from an inactivated bacterial toxin is called a {{c1::toxoid}}.
cards.question: A vaccine antigen derived from an inactivated bacterial toxin is called a {{c1::toxoid}}.

cards.explanation: This targets toxin-mediated disease and need not prevent bacterial carriage.
cards.text: Toxoid vaccination primarily protects by inducing antibodies that {{c1::neutralise the toxin}}.
cards.question: Toxoid vaccination primarily protects by inducing antibodies that {{c1::neutralise the toxin}}.

cards.explanation: An immune response can be directed against a relevant component without administering a whole organism.
cards.text: A vaccine made from selected microbial antigens is called a {{c1::subunit vaccine}}.
cards.question: A vaccine made from selected microbial antigens is called a {{c1::subunit vaccine}}.

cards.explanation: Purified antigens can provide a weaker stimulus on their own.
cards.text: A substance added to enhance the immune response to a vaccine antigen is an {{c1::adjuvant}}.
cards.question: A substance added to enhance the immune response to a vaccine antigen is an {{c1::adjuvant}}.

cards.explanation: The mRNA serves as a temporary template for translation.
cards.text: After mRNA vaccination, the encoded antigen is produced by the recipient’s {{c1::ribosomes}}.
cards.question: After mRNA vaccination, the encoded antigen is produced by the recipient’s {{c1::ribosomes}}.

cards.explanation: This process does not require alteration of the recipient’s genomic DNA.
cards.text: Vaccine mRNA is translated in the {{c1::cytoplasm}}.
cards.question: Vaccine mRNA is translated in the {{c1::cytoplasm}}.

cards.explanation: Memory lymphocytes can respond more rapidly on subsequent exposure.
cards.text: A booster dose re-exposes the immune system to antigen and recalls {{c1::immune memory}}.
cards.question: A booster dose re-exposes the immune system to antigen and recalls {{c1::immune memory}}.

cards.explanation: Broader coverage depends on which types are included.
cards.text: A vaccine designed to cover multiple antigenic types is {{c1::multivalent}}.
cards.question: A vaccine designed to cover multiple antigenic types is {{c1::multivalent}}.

cards.explanation: Several capsular serogroups can cause invasive disease.
cards.text: The bacterium targeted by meningococcal vaccines is {{c1::Neisseria meningitidis}}.
cards.question: The bacterium targeted by meningococcal vaccines is {{c1::Neisseria meningitidis}}.

cards.explanation: The protein enables T-cell help for the antibody response to the polysaccharide.
cards.text: A conjugate vaccine links a capsular polysaccharide to a {{c1::carrier protein}}.
cards.question: A conjugate vaccine links a capsular polysaccharide to a {{c1::carrier protein}}.

cards.text: MenACWY covers meningococcal serogroups {{c1::A, C, W and Y}}.
cards.question: MenACWY covers meningococcal serogroups {{c1::A, C, W and Y}}.

cards.explanation: The population trend did not support MMR as the explanation for the rise, consistent with wider vaccine-safety evidence.
cards.text: In the Yokohama study, autism diagnoses continued to rise after {{c1::MMR vaccination was withdrawn}}.
cards.question: In the Yokohama study, autism diagnoses continued to rise after {{c1::MMR vaccination was withdrawn}}.
